records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] record_for_host compares only URI(host).host against the stored host column, dropping the port, while the validation regex and admin UI explicitly allow stored hosts to carry a :port suffix. A staff member who configures 'example.com:8080' (accepted by the validation regex) gets a record that never matches any referer, because referer hosts never include the port — the configured host is silently inert; conversely a referer on any port (http://example.com:9999) matches the portless stored host, so the port portion of the allowlist is unenforceable in both directions.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The before_validation callbacks use sub! on self.host, which returns nil (raising NoMethodError in the validation chain) when host is nil, and the second sub! strips everything after '/' before format validation so the stored host can never keep a path the UI edit form might show. Saving a host with a nil host attribute (e.g. create with missing params envelope) raises an exception inside validation rather than producing a validation error; on the controller path params[:embeddable_host][:host] nil triggers it, surfacing a 500 where a 4xx validation error belongs.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] There is no UNIQUE constraint or validation on host, and record_for_host resolves duplicates with .first, so the category that wins for an imported topic is nondeterministic. Two admins can add the same host with different categories; which category receives embedded topics then depends on row order, and the client table shows both rows with no error explaining the conflict. A unique index on lower(host) is the real invariant.

records.issue_text: [BUG] record_for_host strips the port from the incoming URL via uri.host but the stored host column is never stripped of its port (before_validation removes only scheme and path, and the validation regex explicitly allows :[0-9]{1,5}), so a host saved as example.com:8080 can never match any referer. An admin adds 'example.com:8080' as allowed host; every embed request from that origin fails host_allowed? and raises InvalidAccess — the configured host silently never works. Conversely the equality lookup matches on bare hostname so a stored bare 'example.com' also authorizes referers on any port, an over-broad match.
